messages.text: Our dad died and left the house in his will. My sister A wants to buy it with her husband at a "family discount". I'm not signing off on that. Our younger sister B could use some money too. Can you help us sort this out?

Mostly. I want a fair financial share and won’t subsidize A’s discounted purchase. B should share in the value too, but I’m not deciding for her. I don’t know the will’s actual terms yet. You can record that.

What matters is having a secure, independent home and being financially independent. Buying it with my husband feels like a way to do that. I’d want the arrangement to feel fair to B and C, but I don’t know what would feel acceptable to them; C hasn’t agreed. I’m not sure what price or discount would be fair yet.

I suppose having my share of the house’s value available sooner would help me get a dance studio started. I’d be uncomfortable with anything being treated as settled before all three of us agree; I’m not sure about the details yet.

Yes, that wording fits. I haven’t seen the will and don’t know who has it. My discomfort is with being expected to accept a discounted sale that cuts into my share. I don’t know what price would be fair yet.
Yes, that wording fits. I haven’t been told the will’s terms, and I don’t know who holds it. C hasn’t agreed, so I know the discount may be a concern for her; I don’t know of any other discomfort.

Yes, that wording fits. I haven’t seen the will’s terms and don’t know who has the document. I still have that concern about settling anything before all three agree, but I can’t speak for my sisters.

O1 could work with an independent valuation and my share paid in full, subject to the will. O2 only if A covers the entire shortfall herself—my share can’t be discounted. O3 doesn’t work for me as an open-ended arrangement. O4 is a reasonable fallback. I’ll ask about the will.

O2 feels closest to workable, if we can agree the discount and I can fund the amount owed to B and C. I’m not ready to say that’s feasible. O1 also might work, but I don’t know if we could afford full value; O3 and O4 don’t give me the house. I’ll ask about the will’s terms.

O1 seems most workable for me, if my share is paid at closing and we all agree. O2 might work too, but I’m unsure how the shortfall would be handled fairly. O3 makes me uneasy because it wouldn’t get me the money soon. None of this is agreement to settle anything before we know the will’s terms and all three agree.

Yes, that wording fits. I’m willing to consider a jointly chosen independent valuation, with the cost shared. I have some discomfort about whether we can afford the full amount, so I wouldn’t want the valuation to imply a commitment to buy.

Yes, I’m willing to share the valuation cost, provided we choose the surveyor together. I’m not committing to a sale; I’d want my share secured and paid at closing, once we know the will’s terms and all agree.

Yes, I’m willing to consider a jointly chosen independent valuer, with the cost shared as agreed. I don’t have a particular discomfort with O1 yet, so long as the valuation isn’t a commitment to buy or settle anything before the will is known and all three of us agree.
Yes, entry 8 fits. I’ll ask the executor or Dad’s lawyer about the will. I agree the valuation shouldn’t imply a commitment to buy or settle anything.
Confirm entry 8: the valuation isn’t a commitment. But O2 doesn’t automatically apply if A can’t fund O1; any alternative still needs all three of us to agree.
Yes, entry 8 fits. One thing: if O1 isn’t affordable, O2 shouldn’t automatically apply; we’d need to discuss it and all three agree.
